label: The pointer belongs in shared/references/workflow-implement.md section 2 Research step 5, not in the sk-code hub SKILL.md: the hub is routing-only by contract and the shared doctrine is the single source each surface packet links and applies.

The precise wording is one appended clause to existing step 5: when the runtime exposes a code-search tool and the project carries .sweet-search/config.json, use ranked search, trace and repo-map for the concept-and-unfamiliar branch, keep literal search for exact text and symbols and path match for known paths, and fall back to widen-pattern-then-read when absent or uninitialized; it is never a prerequisite.

Detection needs no new Skilled script: a three-rung ladder over the MCP tool roster, the local .sweet-search/config.json init marker and the existing sweet-search status --json command (exit 0 ready, 1 missing step) answers installed, initialized and stale.

The pointer must not edit AGENTS.md and slots into the decision tree's concept-and-unfamiliar branch only: the tree is capability-framed, exact text and known paths keep literal search and path match, and the root AGENTS.md is not in the always-linked .skilled set that external installs receive.

A load caveat and a cost finding qualify the recommendation: workflow-implement.md is a declared leaf but not a RESOURCE_MAP entry, so it is reached through the surface packet's workflow instruction; and the clause is paid on every code task whether or not Sweet Search is installed, so iteration 6's demonstrated-need bar still governs.
The sk-code hub stays routing-only; workflow behavior belongs in the shared doctrine, never in SKILL.md.

reason: The hub is routing-only by its own contract, and search behavior is workflow logic, not routing.
The root file is not in the always-linked .skilled set, and a vendor name would make a capability-framed tree tool-specific.
The MCP roster, the .sweet-search/config.json marker and status --json already answer detection with no new maintenance surface.
One doctrine file is enough to test the idea; a second edit doubles the cost before any evidence of need.
